# MCP tools

The tools an agent sees when it connects to memini, generated from the same definitions returned by `tools/list`.

- **Streamable HTTP**, at `http://<host>:8080/mcp`, for a shared always-on server.
- **stdio**, via `memini mcp`, for a server the agent spawns per session.

## The tools

| Tool | Does | Available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`memory_briefing`](#memory_briefing) | Session briefing | always |
| [`memory_recall`](#memory_recall) | Recall memories | always |
| [`memory_remember`](#memory_remember) | Remember a fact | always |
| [`memory_answer`](#memory_answer) | Answer from memory | **only with an LLM configured** |
| [`memory_list`](#memory_list) | Browse memories | always |
| [`memory_get`](#memory_get) | Get a memory | always |
| [`memory_history`](#memory_history) | Trace a memory's history | always |
| [`memory_update`](#memory_update) | Update a memory | always |
| [`memory_forget`](#memory_forget) | Forget a memory | always |

`memory_answer` is only registered when `MEMINI_LLM_BASE_URL` is set.

## Server instructions

```text
memini is persistent cross-session memory for this agent. Namespaces are managed for you — you never construct or type a raw namespace path; you make semantic choices (scope to read, visibility to write) and learn the topology by reading provenance. Standing policy:
- At session start, call memory_briefing once to orient (pinned context, durable facts, how-tos, recent activity, and the inherited Scope line). Prefer it over broad recall queries.
- Before work that may have history, call memory_recall first. scope is "project", "full" (default: project plus ancestors, personal namespace, and links), or "everywhere" (full plus nested sub-projects).
- After learning something durable, call memory_remember proactively: one atomic, self-contained fact per call. Don't store what's already in project docs/CLAUDE.md or trivially recoverable from code.
- visibility decides who should know: "project", "personal", or an ancestor name read from the briefing Scope line. Durable shared facts go up; personal preferences go personal; episodic/working writes always stay in the project.
- tier: semantic = durable fact, procedural = how-to/command, episodic = what happened, working = scratch. Omit to auto-classify.
- Every recall/briefing result carries provenance. Read "from" and the Scope line; never guess namespace paths.
- Tag critical facts "pinned" and set metadata.category to a topic bucket.
- Correct or extend facts with memory_update. memory_forget is only for memories that should not exist. Copy addressing namespaces verbatim from results.
- Empty recall means nothing is known. A degraded field means results are keyword-only and incomplete, not a confident negative.
```

## `memory_briefing`

*read-only*

Layered session-start briefing for this namespace — pinned context, durable facts, how-to procedures, and recent activity — in one query-less call. Call it when a session opens. The scope_header spells out the inherited ancestor chain. scope='everywhere' also includes compact direct-child rollups.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `per_section` | integer |  | default cap for a section whose dedicated cap is unset (default 5) |
| `per_section_facts` | integer |  | max durable semantic facts; 0 disables |
| `per_section_pinned` | integer |  | max pinned memories; 0 disables |
| `per_section_procedures` | integer |  | max procedural memories; 0 disables |
| `per_section_recent` | integer |  | max recent episodic entries; 0 disables |
| `scope` | string |  | how wide to brief: project, full (default), or everywhere One of `project`, `full`, `everywhere`. |

## `memory_recall`

*read-only*

Search prior context via hybrid semantic and keyword retrieval, ranked by relevance, recency, and corroboration. Call BEFORE starting work that may have history. Prefer a short descriptive query. Empty results mean nothing is known; a degraded field means semantic search was unavailable and results are keyword-only. scope is project, full (default), or everywhere. Supports time-travel with as_of and optional LLM query rewriting. Each result's namespace is provenance: copy it verbatim into memory_get/update/forget.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as_of` | string |  | RFC3339 time for time-travel recall |
| `exclude_metadata` | object |  | drops memories matching each supplied key=value pair |
| `include_fresh_turns` | boolean |  | also return this session's just-captured conversation turns |
| `levels` | string[] |  | restrict to levels; empty means all One of `explicit`, `deduced`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | max results (default 10) |
| `metadata` | object |  | only memories whose metadata has each key=value pair (AND) |
| `query` | string | yes | natural-language search text; short and descriptive works best |
| `query_rewrite` | boolean |  | rewrite into variants and fuse via RRF |
| `response_format` | string |  | concise returns summary-or-truncated content; detailed returns full content One of `concise`, `detailed`. |
| `scope` | string |  | how wide to read: project, full (default), or everywhere One of `project`, `full`, `everywhere`. |
| `tags` | string[] |  | only memories carrying every listed tag (AND) |
| `tiers` | string[] |  | restrict to tiers; empty means all One of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic`, `procedural`. |

## `memory_remember`

*additive*

Store a fact, decision, preference, or event for later recall. Call proactively when the user says 'remember this', after an architectural decision (capture the why), after discovering a non-obvious bug or convention, or when a stated preference should outlive this session. Keep memories atomic — one self-contained fact per call; search works better on small records. Do NOT store facts already in project docs/CLAUDE.md or trivially recoverable from code. tier: semantic=durable fact, procedural=how-to, episodic=event, working=scratch (default intake, omit to auto-classify). visibility: 'project' (default) keeps it here; 'personal' follows the user everywhere; or name an ancestor from the briefing Scope line to share it up that chain — episodic/working writes always stay in project regardless. If the result carries merge_hint, call memory_update with id=merge_hint.similar_id to fold them together, or ignore it to keep both. Returns {id, tier, stored}; stored=false means a low-signal write was dropped by the value gate (not an error).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confidence` | number |  | 0..1 seed corroboration for a durable fact; omit for default |
| `content` | string | yes | the fact to store — atomic and self-contained, readable without this conversation's context |
| `id` | string |  | upserts an existing memory when provided |
| `importance` | number |  | 0..1 ranking/retention bias; omit for the default |
| `level` | string |  | provenance: explicit = user-stated, deduced = LLM-inferred; omit to leave unset One of `explicit`, `deduced`. |
| `metadata` | object |  | structured key/values for later filtering; set 'category' to a topic bucket |
| `summary` | string |  | optional one-line summary |
| `tags` | string[] |  | topic labels for filtering and keyword search; tag a critical always-relevant fact 'pinned' so it surfaces in every session briefing |
| `tier` | string |  | working, episodic, semantic, or procedural (omit to auto-classify) One of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic`, `procedural`. |
| `ttl_seconds` | integer |  | overrides the tier default TTL; negative means never expire |
| `valid_from` | string |  | RFC3339 start of the fact's validity; backdate for as_of recall |
| `valid_to` | string |  | RFC3339 end of the fact's validity; omit if still true |
| `visibility` | string |  | who should remember this: project (default), personal, or an ancestor name from the briefing Scope line; episodic/working writes always stay in project |

## `memory_answer`

*read-only*

Recall relevant memories and answer a question grounded on them (requires an LLM). Slower than memory_recall; use when you want a synthesized answer with sources.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | string[] |  | restrict grounding to levels One of `explicit`, `deduced`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | max memories to ground on (default 10) |
| `metadata` | object |  | ground only on memories whose metadata has each key=value pair (AND) |
| `query` | string | yes | the question to answer from memory |
| `reasoning_level` | string |  | effort; higher means iterative search and more latency One of `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. |
| `scope` | string |  | how wide to ground: project, full (default), or everywhere One of `project`, `full`, `everywhere`. |
| `tags` | string[] |  | ground only on memories with every listed tag (AND) |
| `tiers` | string[] |  | restrict grounding to tiers One of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic`, `procedural`. |

## `memory_list`

*read-only*

Browse memories without a query — filter by tier, tags, or metadata. Returns at most limit (default 20) newest-first; page with offset. For relevance-ranked search use memory_recall.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | string[] |  | restrict to levels; empty means all One of `explicit`, `deduced`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | max results (default 20, newest first) |
| `metadata` | object |  | only memories whose metadata has each key=value pair (AND) |
| `namespace` | string |  | tenant namespace; defaults to the server namespace |
| `offset` | integer |  | skip this many results for paging |
| `tags` | string[] |  | only memories carrying every listed tag (AND) |
| `tiers` | string[] |  | restrict to tiers; empty means all One of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic`, `procedural`. |

## `memory_get`

*read-only*

Fetch one memory with full metadata, tags, and timestamps by ID.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | the memory ID |
| `namespace` | string |  | tenant namespace; defaults to the server namespace |

## `memory_history`

*read-only*

Trace a memory's bi-temporal supersession lineage, oldest-first, including tombstoned rows.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | the memory ID |
| `namespace` | string |  | tenant namespace; defaults to the server namespace |

## `memory_update`

*additive*

Update fields of an existing memory by ID. Only provided fields change and metadata merges key-by-key. Use it to correct or enrich a fact; to delete, use memory_forget.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confidence` | number |  | 0..1; omit to keep |
| `content` | string |  | replacement content; omit to keep |
| `id` | string | yes | the memory ID to update |
| `importance` | number |  | 0..1; omit to keep |
| `metadata` | object |  | merged into existing metadata key-by-key |
| `namespace` | string |  | tenant namespace; defaults to the server namespace |
| `summary` | string |  | replacement summary; omit to keep |
| `tags` | string[] |  | replacement tag set; omit to keep |
| `tier` | string |  | move to this tier; omit to keep One of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic`, `procedural`. |

## `memory_forget`

*destructive*

Permanently delete a memory by ID — use for wrong, outdated, or unwanted memories. To correct a fact instead, prefer memory_update so history is preserved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | the memory ID |
| `namespace` | string |  | tenant namespace; defaults to the server namespace |
